definition: Information integration (II) is the merging of information from heterogeneous sources with differing conceptual, contextual and typographical representations.
details: It is used in data mining and consolidation of data from unstructured or semi-structured resources. Typically, information integration refers to textual representations of knowledge but is sometimes applied to rich media content. Information fusion, a related term, involves the combination of information into a new set of information in order to reduce redundancy and uncertainty. Examples of technologies available to integrate information include deduplication and string metrics, which allow the detection of similar text in different data sources by fuzzy matching. Other methods rely on causal estimates of the outcomes based on a model of the sources.

explainer.lead: Information integration merges information from heterogeneous sources that differ in concept, context and typography. It matters because useful data usually arrives from many inconsistent places that must be reconciled.

tiers.eli5: It is like combining several address books written in different formats into one list without creating duplicates or contradictions.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it in data mining and in consolidating unstructured or semi-structured sources, often with deduplication and string-metric techniques. A pitfall is that differing representations of the same fact cause duplicates or inconsistencies unless matching is handled carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Merging of information from heterogeneous sources with differing conceptual, contextual and typographical representations. Related information fusion combines information into a new set to reduce redundancy and uncertainty; technologies include deduplication and string metrics.

explainer.example: Two customer datasets storing names and addresses in different formats are merged, with string metrics and deduplication preventing duplicate records.
